# Independent audit: contact-constrained projective surface cell repair

Audited source:
`candidate e6ba532e542af929`.


coupling with zero `L`-Jensen gap. The source does not claim that the
physical variational stress automatically has that property.

## 1. Contact cells and compactness

For `L=min_i A_i`, each cell `{A_i=L}` is the intersection of the
closed affine halfspaces `A_i<=A_j`. It is convex and closed. The
same statement holds for each plane of the finite support roof.
Both Jensen gaps are nonnegative continuous functions of the two
endpoints. Their zero set is closed in the compact endpoint product,
so fixed-marginal couplings concentrated there form a compact convex
set containing the prescribed old coupling.

If `A_i` is active at the midpoint and the `L`-Jensen gap is zero,
the sum of the two nonnegative endpoint gaps `A_i-L` is zero.
Thus both endpoints lie in the same closed cell. Conversely any
pair in that cell has zero Jensen gap, since the affine upper plane
and the concave lower bound agree at its midpoint. The identical
argument handles the support roof. This remains true for ties and
for different ordered base pairs within one fixed parity class.

## 2. The essential unrestricted-optimizer step

The proof partitions ONE existing constrained surplus maximizer by
the canonical active planes of its output. A piece's restricted
endpoint marginals have support in the corresponding CLOSED contact
cells, even though the canonical Borel part used to define the piece
need not be closed. Their support closures do not leave the cells.

Every coupling of these restricted marginals stays in the product of
the same two closed contact cells. It therefore satisfies both
Jensen equalities and can replace the piece without changing any
global endpoint marginal. It follows that the piece itself is an
unrestricted surplus optimizer for its own marginal pair.

This reasoning would fail if the initial maximization also imposed
the desired old-midpoint convex-order condition: a replacement piece
could violate that condition. The source correctly imposes only
the closed contact conditions during these maximizations, and obtains
old-law convex order later by finite intersection.

## 3. Density and no extra cell factor

On the `i`-th closed cell, the denominator is the single common
affine function `A_i`, positive everywhere on the compact body.
The restricted endpoint measures are dominated by the corresponding
common-affine weighted reference measures. The common numerator's
positive-part convention is valid because both positive weighted
endpoint values lie in its positive concave domain.

The roof-cell equality ensures every product pair of restricted
endpoint supports has an actual tight target face. The common face
dimension, tangent direction, and unique perpendicular target offset
are those of the already audited mixed surface theorem. Thus the
inverse-map and weighted-area proof applies directly to this
restricted optimizer, in the augmented finite-base coordinates if
needed. It establishes the density bound for THAT optimizer, not
merely for an alternative coupling.

The restricted output laws are still the disjoint canonical Borel
parts of the original global optimizer. Their reference ceilings
agree with the actual weight on their respective parts. Summing
their measure inequalities therefore adds no factor for the number
of cells. In particular, positive mass on a tie face is assigned to
one canonical output label, so it is not charged twice. No assertion
that separate replacement couplings retain these labels is used.

## 4. Convex-order selection and boundary cases

The contact-constrained class with the fixed finite target domination
is weakly compact: the contact zero set is closed, and domination by
a fixed finite Borel measure is characterized by closed inequalities
against continuous nonnegative functions. Every smooth strongly
convex surplus maximum over the full contact class is in this capped
subclass by the preceding argument.

Smooth approximation transfers the maximal-value comparison to any
finite convex test. Nonnegative finite separation and compact finite
intersection then provide one capped coupling dominating the
prescribed old midpoint law in convex order. The old coupling's
contact hypothesis is used both for nonemptiness and for this
maximal-value comparison.

For zero-dimensional conditional faces, the inverse-endpoint argument
uses the exact atom minimum bound. The one-dimensional interval case
is supplied by the elementary weighted surface result. No ambient
volume or a nonexistent zero-dimensional surface measure is used.

## 5. Measurable assembly and marks

All final constraints can be stated without any measurable choice of
face frame or roof facet: fixed conditional marginals, zero integral
of the nonnegative continuous `L` gap, fixed weighted target
domination, and countably many convex-order inequalities. The bounded
Borel weight supplies finite Borel target kernels and uniform mass
bounds. Target domination already confines outputs to the actual
normal support graph. The established compact-selector theorem
therefore applies in the original physical coordinates.

The selected old-to-new midpoint martingale and the subsequent
endpoint disintegration preserve the stated marks and conditional
midpoint means. Because both old and new endpoint couplings have
zero `L` gap and identical endpoint marginals, their midpoint laws
have equal `L` integrals. Concavity and the integrated martingale
Jensen equality then give zero `L` gap for this old-to-new midpoint
martingale as claimed.

## 6. The remaining applicability condition is genuine

For a physical stress martingale `nu<=cx eta`, concavity gives only
`integral L dnu >= integral L deta`. Zero gap is an additional
equality. It is equivalent to concentration of every martingale row
in each affine contact cell active at the row's source. An equality
for a distinct inverse-volume contact-row measure does not establish
it for these physical surface marginals.

The audited result resolves the finite-cell overlap problem once that
equality holds. It does not supply the equality or a halfspace-depth
bound, and no such implication is hidden in its proof.
